Motivation
WHO-reported workforce density in Sub-Saharan Africa
1.55 per 1,000
physicians, nurses and midwives per 1,000 population
Physicians alone: 0.2 per 1,000
Low provider density is commonly interpreted as evidence of high workloads.
But implied workload also depends on demand for care.
6 visits/person/year
implies
15.5 patients/provider/day
The right-hand calculation holds provider density at 1.55 per 1,000 population and assumes 250 working days. The point is sensitivity, not that any one utilization rate is the correct one.
We therefore measure caseloads directly.
Provider density is informative about supply, but it does not identify realized workload without utilization and allocation.

Conclusion

There is tremendous unused capacity, because patients, capacity and competence are very unevenly matched.

Expanding the workforce may be necessary in particular places. But workforce stocks alone do not diagnose the constraints on service delivery.
Stocks ≠ workloadsCrowding ≠ system-wide overloadCapacity ≠ effective capacity
Daniels, Das, Gatti & Yi Chang (2026), World Bank Research Observer.
